data.name: Humaam
data.gender_notes: Humaam is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root h-m-m which means to give or to reward. In Islamic context, it represents the concept of reward for good deeds and acts of kindness. The name Humaam carries the meaning “Gift, Reward” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Humaam usually hope their child will grow to embody gift, reward and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name filled with blessings and rewards.
data.etymology: Humaam belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gift, Reward.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Humaam total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_english.name: Humaam
in_english.meaning: Humaam means enthusiastic, energetic, and highly motivated person
in_english.long_meaning: Humaam is an Arabic name that means enthusiastic, energetic, and highly motivated person. It is derived from the Arabic root 'H-M-M' which means 'to be eager' or 'to be enthusiastic'. This name is mentioned in Islamic tradition and signifies a person who is highly motivated and active in their pursuits. The name Humaam is associated with positive personality traits such as being diligent, hardworking, and ambitious.

data.cultural_impact: The name Humaam holds various meanings and associations in Arabic and Islamic culture. Being derived from the Arabic word for giving or rewarding, it carries an underlying connotation of kindness, generosity and philanthropy. The name may also be linked to the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) hadith emphasizing good deeds and charity: "Take up Sadaqah (charity) with your right hand and give it to the poor and needy with your left hand, and don't let your left hand know what your right hand is giving" (Bukhari and Muslim).
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic belief, the name Humaam holds deep spiritual significance as it is reflective of the reward and blessings in God's eyes. It highlights the importance of performing good deeds and acts of kindness, which ultimately brings one closer to God and His divine guidance. The name serves as a constant reminder of the concept of 'Thawab' or reward for pious actions and serving others. It aligns with the Islamic values of selflessness, empathy, and compassion, and encourages one to make a positive impact on the world and in people's lives.
